title: Ray's New Intellectual Arithmetic
sourceTitle: Ray's New Intellectual Arithmetic (Eclectic Educational Series)
author: Joseph Ray
licenseEvidence: Internet Archive scan (raysnewintellec00raygoog) of the American Book Co. printing from Harvard College Library; the copyright page reads 'Copyright, 1877, by Van Antwerp, Bragg & Co.' and the preface is dated May 1877. Published before 1930, so public domain in the USA; archive.org marks it NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Not on Project Gutenberg.
description: Joseph Ray's classic 1877 book of mental arithmetic, the next step after Ray's New Primary Arithmetic. Children reason through short spoken word problems with no paper, moving from the four operations through fractions, measures, ratio and percentage to interest. Each day you read the model solution together, work the book's oral problems aloud, and finish with three practice problems. The full scanned book is free online.
includes: 85 lessons covering all 80 of the book's lessons in 15 units
Link to the exact page of the free scanned book for every lesson
Oral problems with model solutions to say back in full sentences
3 practice problems with answers per lesson

lessons.title: Lesson I: Adding Small Numbers
steps: Act out the first problems with real apples, pennies or marbles
Answer each oral problem and tell why, e.g. "because 4 and 2 are 6"
Learn the words sum and amount and the signs + and =
questions: Sam has 4 marbles and finds 3 more. How many does he have now?
How many are 5 cakes and 2 cakes and 2 cakes?
What is the answer to an addition problem called?
lessons.notes: This is mental arithmetic: problems are worked in the head and answered aloud in full sentences, with a slate only for checking.

lessons.title: Lesson II: Adding Numbers Up to 20
steps: Say each sum the way the model solution does: "Two and four are six; six and one are seven"
Count up by 2s from 4 to 16 and by 3s from 1 to 13
Work the story problems about eggs, tape and apples
questions: What are 7 and 5 and 2?
A girl spent 4 cents for pins and 6 cents for thread, and has 3 cents left. How many cents had she at first?
Name two numbers that make 12 when added.

lessons.title: Lesson III: The Addition Table
steps: Read the addition table aloud, a column at a time
Cover the answers and quiz each other on the 7s, 8s and 9s
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is 8 + 7?
What is 9 + 12?
What is 6 + 6?

lessons.title: Lesson IV: Adding to Larger Numbers
steps: Add 2 to 29, 49, 69 and 99 and notice how the ones spill over into the next ten
Run through the book's drills briskly, answer only
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is 49 + 3?
What is 68 + 7?
What is 9 + 86?
lessons.notes: Children who finished Ray's New Primary Arithmetic may begin here, as the book itself suggests.

lessons.title: Lesson V (part 1): Adding Several Numbers
steps: Add long strings of numbers aloud, keeping a running total as in the model solution
Work problems 1–25
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What are 4 and 8 and 3 and 5?
What are 7 and 9 and 5 and 4?
What are 12 and 11 and 7?

lessons.title: Lesson V (part 2): Story Problems and Counting By
steps: Work the story problems 26–38 aloud
Count by 2s, 3s, 4s and up to 9s, as far as 100 (problems 39–53)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A farmer buys 12 hens, then 9 more, then 6 more. How many hens did he buy?
Counting by 7s from 7, what number comes after 49?
Ben is 9 and Ann is 6. Their father is 20 years older than both their ages put together. How old is he?

lessons.title: Lesson VI: Taking Away
steps: Act out taking away with pennies or apples
Answer the oral problems and tell why ("because 2 from 5 leaves 3")
Learn minuend, subtrahend, difference and the minus sign
questions: Lucy has 11 cents and spends 4. How many are left?
Seven from 15 leaves how many?
In 14 − 6 = 8, which number is the subtrahend?

lessons.title: Lesson VII: The Subtraction Table
steps: Read the subtraction table aloud, a column at a time
Check a few lines backward with addition (9 − 4 = 5, so 5 + 4 = 9)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is 13 − 5?
What is 16 − 7?
What is 20 − 8?

lessons.title: Lesson VIII: Subtraction Problems
steps: Read the model solution about the slate and say it back
Work problems 1–25, answering each in a full sentence
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A man has 30 miles to walk and has gone 17. How far is left?
A boy bought a book for 25 cents and sold it for 18 cents. How much did he lose?
The greater of two numbers is 15 and their difference is 6. What is the smaller?

lessons.title: Lesson IX: Review of Adding and Subtracting
steps: Read the two model solutions (the marbles given away, and the marble game)
Work review problems 1–15
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Jim had 20 marbles. He gave 4 to Al and 7 to Ben. How many had he left?
Two boys each start a game with 15 marbles. At the end one has 21. How many has the other?
A grocer pays $8, $6 and $5 for goods and sells them all for $25. What does he gain?

lessons.title: Lesson X: Adding and Subtracting in a Chain
steps: Work each chain left to right, saying the running answer: "3 minus 2 is 1, plus 1 is 2"
Do problems 1–27 aloud; go back to any you missed
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

lessons.title: Lesson XI: Harder Subtraction Problems
steps: Read the model solution for problem 4 and copy its three steps
Work problems 1–22
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: From the sum of 16 and 9, take the difference between 15 and 8.
What number must be added to 20 to make a sum 10 less than 50?
A man buys a cow for $30, pays $8 for her keep, and sells her for $45. What does he gain?

lessons.title: Lesson XII: Equal Groups
steps: Lay out groups of beans (2 groups of 3, 4 groups of 5) and count the totals
Work the oral price problems 1–22
Learn multiplicand, multiplier, product and the sign ×
questions: At 5 cents each, what do 4 pears cost?
If one peach is worth 6 apples, how many apples are 3 peaches worth?
In 4 × 7 = 28, what is 28 called?

lessons.title: Lesson XIII: The Multiplication Table
steps: Read the multiplication table aloud a few rows at a time
Drill the "Exercises on the Table" (4 times 7, 8 times 6, and so on)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What are 7 times 8?
What are 9 times 6?
What are 12 times 11?
lessons.notes: Spread the table over several days if needed; it is the base for everything that follows.

lessons.title: Lesson XIV: Multiplication Problems
steps: Read the model solution: "7 oranges will cost 7 times 2 cents"
Work problems 1–25, including the travelers going opposite ways and the "one man does it" problems
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: At $6 a barrel, what do 7 barrels of flour cost?
Two boys walk away from each other, one 3 miles an hour and the other 4. How far apart are they after 5 hours?
If 3 men can do a job in 5 days, how long would 1 man take?

lessons.title: Lesson XV: Mixed Problems with Multiplication
steps: Work problems 1–19, saying each step of the solution
Work problems 20–38 and the chained products like 2 times 3 times 4
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Buy 3 pencils at 4 cents and 2 erasers at 5 cents. What is the cost?
Two men walk the same way, one 6 miles an hour and the other 4. How far apart are they after 8 hours?
How many are 2 times 3 times 5?

lessons.title: Lesson XVI: How Many Times?
steps: Share 12 beans into piles of 3 and count the piles
Answer the oral problems 1–26 and tell why
Learn divisor, dividend, quotient and the sign ÷
questions: At 4 cents each, how many apples can you buy for 28 cents?
36 trees stand in 4 equal rows. How many are in each row?
In 20 ÷ 5 = 4, which number is the divisor?

lessons.title: Lesson XVII: The Division Table
steps: Read the division table aloud, a column at a time
Say each line backward as multiplication (56 ÷ 8 = 7 because 7 × 8 = 56)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is 56 ÷ 8?
What is 72 ÷ 9?
What is 84 ÷ 12?

lessons.title: Lesson XVIII: Sharing and Dividing
steps: Read the model solutions for problems 7, 11 and 23
Work problems 1–25
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Five children share 40 cents equally. How much does each get?
If 1 man takes 48 days to do a job, how long would 6 men take?
If 4 men earn $48 in 3 days, how much does each man earn in 1 day?

lessons.title: Lesson XIX: Times As Many
steps: Read the model solutions for problems 4, 8 and 22
Work problems 1–35
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Sixty is how many times 12?
How many oranges at 6 cents each must be given for 9 lemons at 4 cents each?
A man goes 9 miles while a boy goes 4. When the man has gone 54 miles, how far has the boy gone?

lessons.title: Lesson XX: Halves, Thirds, Fourths and More
steps: Cut an apple or paper circles into halves, thirds and fourths

Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: How many thirds in 4 apples?
How many fifths in 6 apples?
How many halves in 9 apples?

lessons.title: Lesson XXI: Writing Fractions

Write on the slate the fractions the book gives in words, then read the printed ones aloud
Sort the book's list into proper and improper fractions
questions: In 3/8, which number is the denominator?
Is 7/5 a proper or an improper fraction?
Write two and three-fourths in figures.

lessons.title: Lesson XXII: Finding a Part of a Number
steps: Read the model solution: 1/3 of $6 is $2, so 2/3 is $4
Work problems 1–23
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What are 2/3 of 12?
If a yard of ribbon costs 10 cents, what do 3/5 of a yard cost?
If 4 pounds of rice cost 20 cents, what do 3 pounds cost?

lessons.title: Lesson XXIII: What Part Is It?
steps: Read the model solution: if $1 buys 1/3 of a yard, $2 buys 2/3
Work problems 1–24
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: 3 is what part of 8?
A melon costs 7 cents. What part of it costs 4 cents?
2/3 of 9 is what part of 10?

lessons.title: Lesson XXIV: Finding the Whole from a Part
steps: Read the model solution about the lemon: 1/3 is 3 cents, so the whole is 9 cents
Work problems 1–25
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: If 1/4 of a pie costs 5 cents, what does the whole pie cost?
If 2/3 of a yard costs 8 cents, what does a yard cost?
12 is 3/4 of what number?

lessons.title: Lesson XXV: Sharing That Leaves Fractions
steps: Share 3 apples between 2 people with a knife and name each share
Work problems 1–29
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Share 7 apples equally between 2 boys. How much does each get?
What is 1/4 of 9?
How many times 3 is 14?

units.title: Unit 6: Changing the Form of Fractions (Lessons XXVI–XXIX)

lessons.title: Lesson XXVI: Mixed Numbers to Improper Fractions
steps: Show 2 1/2 with paper circles and count the halves
Work problems 1–12
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

How many sixths in 5 1/6?

lessons.title: Lesson XXVII: Lowest Terms

Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

lessons.title: Lesson XXVIII: Higher Terms
steps: Fold a paper strip in halves, then fourths, and see that 1/2 = 2/4
Work problems 1–23
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

lessons.title: Lesson XXIX: Common Denominators
steps: Read the note on common and least common denominators

Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

lessons.title: Lesson XXXI: Subtracting Fractions

lessons.title: Lesson XXXII: What Is Left?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIV: Fractions in Buying and Working

questions: If 3 pounds of tea cost $2, what do 2 pounds cost?
What are 3/4 of 7?
If 3 men build a fence in 8 days, how long would 4 men take?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXV: Multiplying Mixed Numbers

Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

steps: Read the model solution about raisins paid for with flour
Work problems 1–23
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Buy 4 boxes of raisins at $2 1/2 a box and pay with flour at $5 a barrel. How many barrels?
Three times 4 2/3 are how many times 7?
How many dozen eggs at 10 cents a dozen will pay for 5 pounds of sugar at 8 cents a pound?

units.title: Unit 8: Fractions of Fractions and Dividing Fractions (Lessons XXXVII–XLIV)

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVII: A Fraction of a Fraction
steps: Cut half an apple into 2 pieces and name one piece
Work problems 1–28
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is 1/2 of 1/3?
What are 2/3 of 3/4?
A man owns 3/4 of a boat and sells 1/3 of his share. What part of the boat does he sell?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXVIII: A Fraction of a Mixed Number
steps: Read the model solution about cloth worth 2 1/2 bushels of wheat
Work problems 1–15
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is 1/2 of 3 1/2?
If 2 yards cost $3 1/2, what do 3 yards cost?
What are 2/3 of 4 1/2?

lessons.title: Lesson XXXIX: Finding the Whole from a Part, Again
steps: Read the model solution about the horse sold at a gain
Work problems 1–28
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A boy gave away 6 marbles, which were 2/5 of all he had. How many had he?
A man sold a horse for $60 and gained 1/5 of its cost. What did it cost?
3/4 of a pole is in the ground and 5 feet are above it. How long is the pole?

lessons.title: Lesson XL: Comparing Parts
steps: Read the model solutions for problems 1, 12 and 14
Work problems 1–32
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: 12 is 3/4 of how many times 4?
2/3 of 18 are how many times 4?
A boy keeps 1/4 of 24 apples and shares the rest equally among 3 friends. How many does each friend get?

lessons.title: Lesson XLI: Dividing by a Fraction
steps: Read the model solutions for problems 1, 5 and 19
Work problems 1–28
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: At $1/2 a yard, how much cloth can you buy for $3?
Divide 3/4 by 3/8.
Divide 2/3 by 3/4.

lessons.title: Lesson XLII: Dividing Mixed Numbers
steps: Read the model solution about 10 1/2 acres shared among 6 children
Work problems 1–17
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Divide 7 1/2 acres equally among 5 children. How much does each get?
If 1 1/2 yards of ribbon cost 9 cents, what does 1 yard cost?
How many are 10 divided by 2 1/2?

lessons.title: Lesson XLIII: How Often Is One Contained in Another?
steps: Read the model solution: change both to improper fractions, then divide
Work problems 1–22

questions: At $3/4 a yard, how many yards can you buy for $6?
How often is 1 1/2 contained in 4 1/2?
6 2/3 is 2/3 of what number?

lessons.title: Lesson XLIV: Handy Parts of a Dozen and a Dollar
steps: Learn the two tables: parts of 12, and parts of 100 (12 1/2 cents = 1/8 of a dollar, 33 1/3 = 1/3, and so on)
Work problems 1–31 with dozens and with prices like 25 or 37 1/2 cents
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What do 2/3 of a dozen shirts cost at $18 a dozen?
What do 24 pounds of soap cost at 12 1/2 cents a pound?
Multiply 36 by 33 1/3.

lessons.title: Lesson XLV: Review of the Four Rules
steps: Work problems 1–12 (adding and subtracting money)
Work problems 13–28 ("if 2 cost so much, what will 7 cost")
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Tom has 15 cents, is given 6 more and then 9 more, and spends 12. How many has he left?
If 3 tons of hay cost $27, what do 5 tons cost?
If 4 horses eat 12 bushels of oats in a week, how many bushels will 7 horses eat?

lessons.title: Lesson XLVI (part 1): Review of Fractions
steps: Work review problems 1–18
Work review problems 19–36
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What are 5/8 of 40?
From 7 1/2 take 3 2/3.
If 3 kegs cost $1 1/2, what do 5 kegs cost?

lessons.title: Lesson XLVI (part 2): Review of Fractions
steps: Work review problems 37–52
Work review problems 53–68
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A girl had 30 cents and spent 2/5 of them on 3 pencils. What did each pencil cost?
If 4 men can do a job in 9 days, in how many days can 6 men do it?
6 is what part of 3/4 of 32?

lessons.title: Lesson XLVI (part 3): Review — Overtaking, Cisterns and Shares
steps: Work review problems 69–79
Work review problems 80–93 (overtaking, cisterns, working together)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A is 20 miles ahead of B. B goes 9 miles a day and A goes 5. In how many days will B catch A?
A tank holding 30 gallons fills at 8 gallons an hour and drains at 3 gallons an hour. How long does it take to fill?
A can do a job in 3 days and B in 6 days. How long will they take together?

units.title: Unit 10: Money, Measures and Time (Lessons XLVII–LIII)

lessons.title: Lesson XLVII: United States Money
steps: Learn the table: mills, cents, dimes, dollars, eagles
Handle real coins: 10 pennies for a dime, 10 dimes for a dollar
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: How many mills in 5 cents?
How many cents in 4 dollars?
70 cents are how many dimes?

lessons.title: Lesson XLVIII: Dry Measure
steps: Learn the table: 2 pints = 1 quart, 8 quarts = 1 peck, 4 pecks = 1 bushel
Measure dry beans or rice with a pint and a quart cup
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: How many quarts in 3 pecks?
Change 2 pk. 3 qt. to quarts.
Change 19 pints to quarts.

lessons.title: Lesson XLIX: Liquid Measure
steps: Learn the table: 4 gills = 1 pint, 2 pints = 1 quart, 4 quarts = 1 gallon
Pour water between a pint jar, a quart jar and a gallon jug
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: How many pints in 3 gallons?
How many gills in 2 quarts?
Change 2 gal. 3 qt. to quarts.

lessons.title: Lesson L: Avoirdupois Weight
steps: Learn the table: 16 drams = 1 ounce, 16 ounces = 1 pound, 100 pounds = 1 hundred-weight, 20 hundred-weights = 1 ton
Weigh a few things on a kitchen scale in pounds and ounces
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: How many ounces in 3 pounds?
How many pounds in 3/4 of a hundred-weight?
8 ounces are what part of a pound?
lessons.notes: The scan misprints the pound as "10 ounces" in places; it is 16 ounces.

lessons.title: Lesson LI: Long Measure
steps: Learn the table: inches, feet, yards, rods, furlongs, miles
Measure a room in feet and yards with a tape
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: How many feet in 4 yards?
How many rods in a mile?
How many inches in 2/3 of a yard?

lessons.title: Lesson LII: Time and the Calendar
steps: Learn the time table and the rhyme "Thirty days have September"
Work the problems on parts of a minute, hour, day and week
Count days between dates on a real calendar (problems 15–21)
questions: How many minutes in 3/4 of an hour?
6 hours are what part of a day?
How many days in June, July and August together?

lessons.title: Lesson LIII: Problems with Measures
steps: Work problems 1–11 (pricing goods by measure)
Work problems 12–21 (wheels, trains and fences)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: At 40 cents a bushel, what do 2 bu. 2 pk. of corn cost?
When milk is 4 cents a pint, what do 2 gallons cost?
A wheel goes 2 yd. 1 ft. in one turn. How far does it go in 6 turns?

units.title: Unit 11: General Review: Harder Problems (Lessons LIV–LIX)

lessons.title: Lesson LIV: Review Problems in Money
steps: Work problems 1–9
Work problems 10–17
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A man buys a horse for $95 and sells him for $130. What does he gain?
What do 4 yards cost at $1 and 25 cents a yard?
If a boat sails 45 miles in 9 hours, how far will it sail in 4 hours?

lessons.title: Lesson LV: Review Problems in Fractions
steps: Read the model solution for problem 2 and say each step
Work problems 1–34
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: If 1/3 of a yard costs $2, what will 3/4 of a yard cost?
If 2/3 of a ton of hay cost $12, what will 1/2 a ton cost?
John has 12 marbles, and 1/2 of John's marbles equal 2/3 of James's. How many has James?

lessons.title: Lesson LVI: Sums and Differences
steps: Read the model solution: twice the greater number is the sum plus the difference
Work problems 1–31
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: The sum of two numbers is 20 and their difference is 6. What are the numbers?
Divide 24 into two parts so that the second is 3 times the first.
If 4 is added to 3 times a number, the sum is 25. What is the number?

lessons.title: Lesson LVII: Dividing into Parts by Fractions
steps: Read the model solutions for problems 1, 6 and 21
Work problems 1–26, including the clock puzzles
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Divide 20 into two parts so that the smaller is 2/3 of the larger.

Divide 21 into two parts so that the smaller is 3/4 of the larger.

lessons.title: Lesson LVIII: A Number and Its Parts
steps: Read the model solution: a number plus its half is 3/2 of the number
Work problems 1–15
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A number plus its half is 18. What is the number?
Ann spent 2/5 of her money and had 30 cents left. How much had she at first?
A number doubled and increased by its half makes 25. What is the number?

lessons.title: Lesson LIX: Working Together
steps: Read the model solutions for problems 10 and 14
Work problems 1–19
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check

steps: Read the model solutions for problems 1 and 10
Work problems 1–19
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: 3 is what per cent of 12?
Of 40 pupils, 30 are present. What per cent are present?
A hat bought for $5 is sold for $6. What per cent is gained?

lessons.title: Lesson LXVIII: Finding the Cost from the Selling Price
steps: Read the model solution: a 20 per cent gain makes the price 6/5 of the cost
Work problems 1–20
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A watch sold for $18 brought a gain of 20 per cent. What did it cost?
A horse sold for $27 brought a loss of 10 per cent. What did it cost?
Goods sold for $35 brought a gain of 25 per cent. What did they cost?

lessons.title: Lesson LXIX: Discounts Off the List Price
steps: Learn what "10 per cent off" and "20 and 5 off" mean
Work problems 1–10
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A $5 book is sold at 20 per cent off. What is paid?
A $200 bill of goods is sold at 1/4 off. What is paid?
A $100 bill is sold at "20 and 5 off". What is paid?

units.title: Unit 14: Commission, Insurance and Interest (Lessons LXX–LXXIX)

lessons.title: Lesson LXX: Commission
steps: Learn what commission is: pay to an agent for buying or selling
Work problems 1–8
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: An agent sells a house for $2000 at 3 per cent commission. What is his commission?
An agent sells $400 of goods at 5 per cent. How much does the owner receive?
A collector's 10 per cent commission came to $30. How much did he collect?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXI: Insurance
steps: Learn the words policy and premium
Work problems 1–6
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is the premium on a $1000 policy at 2 per cent?
A $4000 house is insured for 3/4 of its value at 1 per cent. What is the premium?
What is the premium on $600 at 1/2 per cent?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXII: Interest by Years
steps: Learn interest, principal and amount
Work problems 1–10: find the per cent for all the years, then take that part of the principal
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Find the interest of $10 for 2 years at 5 per cent.
Find the interest of $50 for 3 years at 6 per cent.
Find the interest of $40 for 4 years at 5 per cent.

lessons.title: Lesson LXXIII: Interest for Months and Days
steps: Read the model solutions; count a year as 12 months of 30 days
Work problems 1–21, including the amount (principal plus interest)
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: Find the interest of $60 for 6 months at 6 per cent.
Find the interest of $100 for 3 months at 8 per cent.
What is the amount of $50 for 2 years at 6 per cent?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXIV: Finding the Principal
steps: Read the model solution: if 12/100 of the principal is $3, the principal is $25
Work problems 1–8
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: The interest for 2 years at 5 per cent is $4. What is the principal?
What principal at 6 per cent gives $12 interest a year?
What principal at 4 per cent for 5 years gives $10 interest?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXV: Principal from the Amount
steps: Read the model solution: at 10 per cent the amount is 11/10 of the principal
Work problems 1–7
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What principal at 5 per cent for 2 years amounts to $66?
What principal at 10 per cent for 3 years amounts to $130?
What principal at 4 per cent for 5 years amounts to $60?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXVI: Finding the Time
steps: Read the model solutions, including how long money takes to double
Work problems 1–10
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: In what time, at 5 per cent, will $40 give $6 interest?
In what time does money double at 10 per cent?
In what time, at 4 per cent, will $50 give $3 interest?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXVII: Finding the Rate
steps: Read the model solution: find one year's interest, then what part of the principal it is
Work problems 1–10
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: At what per cent will $100 give $12 interest in 2 years?
At what per cent will $50 give $8 interest in 4 years?
At what per cent will money double itself in 20 years?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXVIII: Present Worth and Discount
steps: Learn present worth and discount: interest paid in advance
Work problems 1–12
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: What is the present worth, at 5 per cent, of $60 due in 4 years?
What is the discount on that same note?
What is the present worth, at 10 per cent, of $90 due in 5 years?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXIX: Interest Puzzles
steps: Work problems 1–8 (what part of the principal the interest is)
Work problems 9–14
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: At 5 per cent for 4 years, the interest is what part of the principal?
When the interest for 2 years is 1/10 of the principal, what is the rate?
In what time at 5 per cent will a principal give the same interest as in 2 years at 10 per cent?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXX (part 1): Miscellaneous Problems
steps: Work problems 1–10
Work problems 11–20, using the model solutions for the beggars and the hare and hound
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: If 3 pears are worth 6 apples, and 2 apples are worth 8 plums, how many plums should be given for 4 pears?
Five times a number is 12 more than 3 times the number. What is the number?
If a father gives each child 2 peaches he has 6 left; if he gives each 4 he has none left. How many children has he?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXX (part 2): Miscellaneous Problems
steps: Work problems 21–30
Work problems 31–40
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A chain cost 1/2 as much as a watch, and both cost $30. What did the watch cost?
Mary gives each playmate 4 cherries and has 10 left; to give each 6 she would need all of them. How many playmates?
Tom is 4 times as old as James, and the difference of their ages is 12 years. How old is each?

lessons.title: Lesson LXXX (part 3): Miscellaneous Problems
steps: Work problems 41–50, using the model solution about the idle laborer
Work problems 51–61
Solve the 3 practice problems below aloud, then check
questions: A worker earns $2 for each day he works and pays $1 for each idle day. After 10 days he has $14. How many days was he idle?
A is 3 times as old as B, and B is twice as old as C. A is 25 years older than C. How old is each?
Selling sugar at 8 cents a pound loses 20 cents; selling at 10 cents a pound gains 20 cents. How many pounds are there?
lessons.notes: The book's last pages are puzzle problems; it is fine to spread this lesson over extra days.
